summary: The common-coset power completion, the strict zero-avoidance shift, the quadratic-jet degree bookkeeping, the quadratic character-sum count and the adaptive pass bound all check out, and every live score I compared (108/110, 102/102 to 109/109, 118/118 to 124/122, 31/29 to 31/30, 344 witnesses, 16 stages, 1934 proposals, 11 moves, 116319 Horner evaluations) matches the artifact. The one defect is the tight-degree counterexample. It is stated without the coset orientation, and it is false for the nonsquare coset. Brute force over F5 with shifts (0,0,0,1) and K=2 gives 0 perfect strict polynomials for the square coset but 1 for the nonsquare coset. Nothing load-bearing is shown wrong.

claims.quote: Thus ALL common-coset inputs are solved perfectly
claims.finding: With F=W-T/beta of degree rD and leading coefficient lambda^r, the polynomial part R of F^(1/r) gives deg(R^r-F)<(r-1)D, Q=beta(R^r-F), and Q(a_i)-t_i=beta*R(a_i)^r because V(a_i)=0. This needs r invertible mod p (true since r|p-1) and the zero-including convention, which the section assumes. The artifact thresholds agree: N127,K77 and N31,K16 (r=2), r=3 N63,K46 and r=4 N32,K24 global inputs are all perfect.

claims.quote: Under independent shifts at unseen coordinates the one-trial expected score fraction approaches rho+R below the perfect threshold
claims.finding: Forcing M about rK/(r-1) positions and scoring the rest with membership density near 1/r gives rR/(r-1)+(1/r)(1-rR/(r-1)) = R+1/r. The note correctly limits this to an IID expectation.

claims.quote: Hence K>=b+1 is a uniform sufficient condition for perfect STRICT common-coset completion
claims.step: Strict Nonzero Powers: Constructive Zero Avoidance
claims.finding: Q_new-Q=beta((R+c)^r-R^r) has degree at most (r-1)D=b and Q has degree below b, so deg Q_new<=b. Choosing c among 0..M avoids the at most M values -R(a_i), since M<p. The artifact's strict controls record proved_degree_dimension_threshold=b+1 (65, 43, 25), and the six seeded siblings plus four traps are perfect. The r=4 sibling uses K=25, not the K=24 of the zero-including control.

claims.quote: all25 native polynomials fail perfect strict satisfaction
claims.step: Strict Nonzero Powers: tight degree paragraph (p5,N4,K2,r2)
claims.finding: The statement omits the coset orientation, and the result depends on it. Over F5 with points 1..4 and shifts (0,0,0,1), K=2 has 0 perfect strict polynomials for the square coset (orientation 0, the case the test uses) but exactly 1 for the nonsquare coset (orientation 1). It is a valid counterexample only once orientation 0 is stated.

claims.quote: Uniform proposals therefore succeed with probability>=1/3
claims.finding: For a!=0, sum_z chi(a+beta z^2)=-chi(beta), so the accepted count including zeros is (p-chi(beta/beta_i)+Z)/2 >= (p-1)/2, and (p-1)/(2p)>=1/3 for p>=3. The h/f bookkeeping keeps deg(2R0 L+L^2)<K. When M=2K, f becomes 0 and the artifact reports NO_FREE_JET_COORDINATES for the global K39 inputs, which is consistent.

claims.quote: For N127,K39 mixed inputs,102/102 improves to109/109. For N127,K77,118/118 improves to124/122.
claims.step: Adaptive Root-Value Exchange Is Now Executed
claims.finding: The artifact repair records match: initial 102 and 102 to final 109 and 109 for K39, and 118 and 118 to 124 and 122 for K77, all ending NO_SAMPLED_IMPROVEMENT. Totals: 16 repair stages, 1934 proposals, 11 accepted moves, 116319 Horner evaluations. The pass bound N-initial_score+1 follows because every non-final pass makes a strict improvement.

summary: The norm construction (Q=Q0+R^2 with F=R^2-nu Z^2) satisfies both coset groups, and the degree budget K>max(|A|,D) is correct. Norm representability through the odd-degree-irreducible parity rule and the Cayley norm-one rotation for strict roots are both valid. I recomputed the p=23 all-parameter counterexample with FLINT: V_A-V_B=16X^3+14X^2+4X, the base target is X^4+21X^3+6X^2, and none of the 23 monic-pencil targets is a norm. The IID first-trial population bound I_p(D)/p^D follows from the uniform-monic-target argument. The artifact matches 127/127 in 1 and 15 trials at degrees 69 and 64, with K39 not applicable (needs K=70 or 65).

claims.quote: Thus a monic polynomial is a norm exactly when every odd-degree irreducible has even multiplicity.
claims.finding: An irreducible of degree d over Fp splits over F_(p^2) exactly when d is even. Odd-degree irreducibles stay inert and have norm f^2. Scaling by rho in Fp contributes rho^2, so F=N(rho H)=R^2-nu Z^2.

claims.quote: Thus NONE of the23 parameters is a norm, although OPI itself is easy.
claims.step: Try To Disprove The Pencil, Then Repair It
claims.finding: Independent FLINT recomputation agrees. Q=13 is a perfect strict witness (13 is a square, and 17,14,5,7 divided by 5 are squares mod 23). F_lambda=D0*(X/16-lambda) has the three simple roots 0, 9 and 16 plus one moving root, so at most one becomes a double root. All 23 lambda fail the norm test.

claims.quote: At most2N parameters are forbidden. For p>2N, one of 0,...,2N works.
claims.step: Strict Roots Without A Field-Size Search
claims.finding: alpha_s has norm (1-nu s^2)/(1-nu s^2)=1, and the denominator never vanishes because nu is a nonsquare. The numerators (1+nu s^2)R+2 nu s Z and 2sR+(1+nu s^2)Z are nonzero quadratics in s whenever (R,Z)!=(0,0), which holds once F is nonzero at native points. That gives at most 2 bad s per native point.

claims.quote: Interpolation is a linear bijection, so F/rho^2 is a uniform monic degree-D polynomial.
claims.finding: Given the A shifts, lambda and rho, the B residues (plus a uniform auxiliary value) are uniform on D points. F0/rho^2 is then uniform of degree <D, and adding the monic V_B gives a uniform monic degree-D target. Every irreducible even-degree target is a norm and has no Fp root, so the I_p(D)/p^D bound follows. The F11 calibration has I_11(2)=55.

claims.quote: For p>2N the elementary irreducible-count bound gives at least1/(2N).
claims.finding: I_p(D)/p^D >= 1/(2D), and the degree budget D<K forces D<N whenever K<=N. The note never states K<=N, but it is the implicit RS regime: for K>N the problem is trivial by interpolation.

claims.quote: The unchanged N127,K77 seeds29/71 now have perfect127/127 classical witnesses
claims.finding: The artifact shows CLASSICAL_NATIVE_PERFECT_WITNESS with score 127 for both K77 patterns, in both zero-including and strict modes, with 1 and 15 trials and degrees 69 and 64. The sufficient dimensions are 70 and 65, which is why K39 is NOT_APPLICABLE_DEGREE_BUDGET. The norm target degrees 58 and 64 match the quoted roughly 1/58 and 1/64 bounds.

summary: The certificate machinery is valid as written. The PSC degradation isometry (overlap a to d tensor a/d), rounding herald mass to overlap-one flags, and the identity between the source posterior-magnitude recursion and the BPQM heralded pure-state recursion together make the rounded means upper bounds on m_i, and TV<=sum_F m_i follows from the companion hybrid bound. All table rates, the 3/8 follow-up TV 0.0234306, the N32768 TV 0.0102208 and the work counts (65534 combinations, 1008335816 pair visits) match the artifacts. The gap is the wording that the single-length N32768 certificate removes the public-set premise for a half-rate family. The only half-rate set certified is at one length, and the coarse half-rate rows at N<=4096 all fail, so no family with vanishing epsilon_F is exhibited.

claims.quote: The preceding hybrid argument gives average uniform-sign Gibbs TV at most 2 epsilon_F = sum_F m_i.
claims.finding: With epsilon_F=(1/2)sum m_i, this matches the companion note's E_uniform-s TV<=eps+delta<=2 eps, which I checked. The producer sets frozen_prefix_bias_sum_upper=total/2 and the TV bound to total, which is consistent.

claims.quote: In particular m_i equals the UNSQUARED root Uhlmann fidelity of the reversed synthesized CQ bit-channel.
claims.finding: The source minus step (magnitude ab) matches the CQ product-state overlap ab. The source plus mixture ((a+b)/(1+ab) and |a-b|/(1-ab), weights (1+ab)/2 and (1-ab)/2) matches the BPQM check-node heralded mixture, from the same base overlap c. The mean overlap of a heralded mixture is its root fidelity. The N2 artifact shows biases [0.4225,0.65] against reversed fidelities [0.65,0.4225].

claims.quote: The computed mean overlaps are therefore upper bounds on the true m_i.
claims.step: Certified Finite Construction / physical PSC degradation
claims.finding: |psi_x(a)> to |psi_x(d)> tensor |psi_x(a/d)> preserves the Gram matrix, so it is an isometry and PSC(a) degrades to PSC(d). Channel combining preserves degradation order, and fidelity cannot fall under degradation. Rounding overlaps up and moving discarded mass to overlap one are therefore valid upper-bounding steps. The note correctly avoids scalar stochastic ordering.

claims.quote: A clearly labelled post-exploration rate3/8 follow-up at N4096 has certified average TV<=0.023431.
claims.finding: The artifact's 3/8 follow-up TV upper is 15572296433414267196016611094728593/664613997892457936451903530140172288 = 0.0234306. The table's maxima 16, 78, 361 and 1614 and their rates match the artifact, and 3/8>0.35=1-c.

claims.quote: The larger G=256,r=3,b=96 calculation succeeds at N32768, |F|=16384
This finite result removes the missing public-set construction premise for the stated half-rate family.
claims.finding: Half rate is certified at only one length (N=32768, TV<=0.0102). At G=64 every half-rate row (N=16..4096) fails, and no length sequence with epsilon_F->0 is certified. The premise in the companion note needs epsilon_F->0 with a polynomial construction, so calling one finite certificate a family over-reaches. The next sentence concedes there is no fixed-grid asymptotic theorem. The not-claimed list and self-check do not narrow the family wording.

summary: The Gibbs mapping is correct: y=E xor J, s=H_F J, and weight proportional to prod(1+c(-1)^(y_j+J_j)) with p=(1-c)/2. The reverse hybrid gives TV(P_U,Qjoint)<=epsilon_F. Under Qjoint, U_F is exactly uniform and Qjoint conditioned on s equals the sampler law Q_s, so the triangle inequalities give the uniform-syndrome and native-syndrome averages <=eps+delta<=2eps. Full row rank makes uniform signs give uniform syndromes. Prefix exactness, the Pinsker/Jensen entropy bound and the reversed CQ/source identity check out, and every table entry matches the artifact (0.4/0.72, 0, 0, 0.00416611/0.05596208).

claims.quote: Thus TV(P_U,Qjoint)<=epsilon_F.
claims.step: Average-Syndrome Guarantee, Not A Worst-Case Guarantee
claims.finding: This is the standard chain-rule hybrid: TV <= sum over i in F of E_P TV(P(U_i|prefix), fair) = sum E|P(U_i=1|prefix)-1/2|. For N=2, F={1}, p=1/10 I recomputed epsilon_F=0.82*(1/2-1/82)=0.4, which matches the artifact's 2/5.

claims.quote: The syndrome marginal discrepancy delta=TV(P_(U_F),Uniform) is at most that joint discrepancy.
claims.step: Average-Syndrome Guarantee, Not A Worst-Case Guarantee
claims.finding: Under Qjoint each frozen bit is a fair coin independent of its prefix, so Qjoint = Uniform(s) x Q_s. Then E_unif TV(Q_s,P_s) = TV(U x Q, U x P_s) <= TV(Qjoint,P_U) + TV(P_U, U x P_s) = eps + delta, and the native average follows the same way. The artifact values satisfy the bound, e.g. N8 {0,1,2,4}: average 0.00417 <= 2*0.2837.

claims.quote: Uniform clause signs give uniform syndromes because H_F has full row rank
claims.step: Average-Syndrome Guarantee, Not A Worst-Case Guarantee
claims.finding: G is invertible, so H_F (rows of G) has full row rank and s=H_F J is uniform for uniform J. The Gibbs TV depends on J only through s, since y=E xor J is a bijection.

claims.quote: For a contiguous initial frozen prefix, however, the remaining chain is already conditioned on every constraint, so sampling is EXACT
claims.finding: With F a prefix, P(U|U_F=s) = prod over free i of P(u_i|u_<i), which is exactly the sampler law. The artifact shows 0 TV at every syndrome for N4 {0,1} and N8 {0,1,2}. For p=1/2 every conditional is fair, so exactness holds for any F.

claims.quote: Hence the CQ information at i equals the source conditional entropy at N-1-i.
claims.step: Why This Is Relevant To The Quantum Proposal
claims.finding: For Arikan F=[[1,0],[1,1]], F^T = R F R holds and extends to tensor powers. The N2 artifact gives Holevo [0.47093,0.86710] against source entropies [0.86710,0.47093], reversed, with identity errors <=6.7e-16, inside the stated 2e-12. The note limits these checks to small cases.

claims.quote: If the corresponding source set has epsilon_F->0 with a polynomial construction, a claimed uniform-random-sign Gibbs advantage is removed by this classical algorithm.
claims.step: Why This Is Relevant To The Quantum Proposal
claims.finding: This follows from the 2 epsilon_F average bound and the polynomial sampler: O(N^2) rational operations, with tests confirming (N-|F|)(2N-1) recursive calls. The note restricts it to uniform signs and does not claim worst-case signs.
